text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"surface_treatment","page":1,"quote":"IZBP"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D23","page":1,"quote":"-0.036"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D24","page":1,"quote":"-0.043"}],"comment":"The shaft carries an IZBP plating (title block, page 1) and the cross-hole tolerances on D23 (-0.036 mm) and D24 (-0.043 mm) are under 0.1 mm, yet no note or dimension accounts for the added plating thickness. The plated holes will be undersize, preventing pins from fitting; the designer must either enlarge the pre-plate hole sizes or add a note to ream after plating.","recommended_correction":"Increase the pre-plate hole dimensions by twice the maximum plating thickness, or add a note specifying that holes are to be finished after plating."},{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N2","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE:- 1) TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 28-32 HRC. 2) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT 3) REMOVE ALL SHARP EDGES & CORNERS."}],"comment":"Note N2 specifies hardness and that threads must stay soft but does not state at which manufacturing stage the heat treatment is applied relative to machining, threading, and the IZBP surface treatment. Without a defined sequence the shop cannot plan operations correctly, risking distortion of finished features or damage to the coating; the designer should add the process order.","recommended_correction":"Add the sequence of operations to N2, e.g., rough machine, heat treat, finish machine, thread, then plate."}]}
